request.principle: Preferred production lip-sync (Dan, 2026-10-30): use local LTX Fast A2V with short source-bound speaking sections, aiming for three seconds and never exceeding four seconds of speech per section. Split at natural pauses. Start the first clip from its approved shot-appropriate canon reference, then generate each continuation sequentially from the previous clip's last retained frame, not the padded native tail. Preserve native reference framing without progressive crop zoom; retain approved canon separately from derived frames and log source video/frame/hash provenance. The tested native minimum is five seconds: pad only the input tail with silence and select only the intended short picture interval. Stitch picture on the unchanged source clock over one continuous original full-line audio track; no inserted lead, audio shift, speed change, speech crossfade, added word or repeated/omitted source sample. Remove generated text and review the full assembled line for sync, pause behavior, speaking coverage, identity/clothing, expression and visible joins through existing production/QC. Carry-over is initial-image conditioning, not hard frame locking; later motion/expression may still drift. Keep existing source/canon/cost/acceptance and designated-speaker constraints. Follow docs/production/LTX_LIPSYNC_EXPERIMENT.md. The verified standalone procedure supports this; the automatic voice/lip-sync stage still constructs KlingLipSyncProvider and needs integration. Selecting ordinary LTX scene motion does not switch lip-sync; do not claim automatic implementation or silently invoke paid fallback.
request.rationale: Explicit producer preference after accepted short Jesus/Peter trials and the Peter frame-chain result. Three-/four-second speech clips worked; five-second/longer speaking tests failed. This records guidance, not automatic-stage migration, new canon approval, blanket take acceptance or new speech.
